corrections.wrong: Said `$binop_(t, binop, c_1, c_2)` "is defined: `∃ lst, fun_binop_ ... lst`". But `lst : Option (List num_)` may be `none` (catch-all case 38, "undefined"), so the statement does not say "defined". `binop_not_none` is what excludes `none`, and `t_progress_be_binop` uses both lemmas.
corrections.fixed: Now says the relation has an output, `lst : Option (List num_)`. The statement alone allows `lst = none`, and `binop_not_none` rules it out. `t_progress_be_binop` uses the two lemmas.

corrections.wrong: Same overclaim: "`$relop_(...)` is defined: `∃ c, fun_relop_ ... c`", although `c = none` is allowed. `relop_not_none` excludes it.
corrections.fixed: Now says the relation has an output. `c = none` is not excluded here; `relop_not_none` excludes it. `t_progress_be_relop` uses both.

corrections.wrong: Same overclaim: "`$cvtop__(...)` is defined: `∃ c2, ...`", although `c2 = none` is allowed. `cvtop_not_none` excludes it.
corrections.fixed: Now says the relation has an output. `c2 = none` is not excluded here; `cvtop_not_none` excludes it. `t_progress_be_cvtop` uses both.

corrections.wrong: Two errors. (1) "`C` is `C'` extended with `F`'s locals, labels and return": `upd_local_label_return C' (map typeof f.LOCALS) lab ret` overwrites three record fields. Locals become the types of F's locals; labels and return are arbitrary `lab`/`ret`, not F's. (2) "Then the sequence is not all constants and steps": the motive concludes `const_list [be] = true ∨ steps`, and the proof takes the step disjunct.
corrections.fixed: Rewritten. C is C' with its locals set to the types of F's locals and its labels/return set to arbitrary `lab`/`ret`. Added the `not_lf_br`/`not_lf_return` hypotheses. The motive concludes "all constants, or steps", and the proof shows it steps.

corrections.wrong: "now every clause has an explicit size argument": the catch-all case 38 has none.
"All `fun_relop_` clauses gained a size argument": the catch-all case 24 did not.

Did not say that the float branch's old pattern `⟨F1, x1, hw1, h1⟩` also shifts: `hw1` binds `var_0` and `h1` the `fun_sizenn` premise, so `numF _ _ h1` is ill-typed. This is outside the first-error list.
corrections.fixed: Added this as a further consequence, before the existing `constructor`/`fun_sizenn`-goal point.

corrections.wrong: Same omission: the float (or float-source) branches' `numF _ _ h1` also fails because of the pattern shift.
corrections.fixed: Added a short note to each, marked as outside the first reported errors.

corrections.wrong: "the model lemma `iadd__is_wf` … `ishr__is_wf`": only iadd/isub/imul are model theorems; iand, ior, ixor, irotl, irotr, ishl, ishr are model axioms.
corrections.fixed: "the model's `iadd__is_wf` … `ishr__is_wf` (theorems for add, sub and mul; axioms for the other seven)".

corrections.wrong: Wrote `…_case_1 _ _ hs2 hs1 hsz` for both REINTERPRET branches, but the float-to-int constructor is `cvtop__Fnn_1_Inn_2_case_2`. Also said the matching widths use "the unchanged clauses 28-35"; only 28/31 (int to float) and 32/35 (float to int) can apply, since 29/30/33/34 have false width premises.
corrections.fixed: Named `cvtop__Inn_1_Fnn_2_case_1` and `cvtop__Fnn_1_Inn_2_case_2`, and said the proof uses clause 28 or 31, or 32 or 35.

corrections.wrong: "every payload `F.const x` (`mk_num__1 F x`)" mixes up the instruction `F.const x` with the number `mk_num__1 F x`.
corrections.fixed: "every number `mk_num__1 F x` (the payload of `F.const x`)".

corrections.wrong: The list of users left out the vector loads and stores: vload_val, vload_pack, vload_splat, vload_zero, vload_lane, vstore and vstore_lane all use it for the address.
